get.summary:
`GET /apps` — the full catalogue in display order. Gating is applied by the
host (the slice exposes one router; there is no longer an ungated public
surface here).

200.description: Every app in the registry, ordered by position

post.summary: `POST /apps` — create a cloud app. Owner-gated by the host.

`POST /apps/{id}` — launch an app (`404` if no app has this id). See the
module docs for the resolve-then-dispatch flow and the auth posture.

204.description: Host sink opened the launch URL for a loopback caller (no redirect)

302.description: Redirect (Location header) to the resolved launch URL

401.description: A loopback launch whose caller is not the device owner

503.description: No reachable launch target (forwarded launch with no public host, or a requires_tunnel app while the tunnel is down)

delete.summary:
`DELETE /apps/{id}` — remove a cloud app or an uploaded self-hosted app.
Owner-gated by the host.

409.description: The app exists but is not removable (system / seeded self-hosted apps)

patch.summary: `PATCH /apps/{id}` — partial update of a cloud app. Owner-gated by the host.

409.description: The app exists but is not a cloud app (system / self-hosted apps are not editable)

put.summary:
`PUT /home-screen` — atomically reorder + enable/disable every app. Owner-gated
by the host. The body must list **every** registry app exactly once (its order
is the new display order); a missing / duplicated / unknown id is
`400 InvalidHomeScreen`. Returns the resulting catalogue in its new order.

200.description: The whole catalogue in its new order

400.description: The body wasn't an exact permutation of the registry

post.summary:
`POST /self-hosted-apps` — install an uploaded zip bundle. Owner-gated by the
host; the body limit is raised to 64 MiB for just this route.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Human app name; also the source of the slugged id/subdomain.

requestBody.description: The app's static files as a zip archive

400.description: Empty/unusable name (`InvalidName`) or a bad bundle (`InvalidZip`)

AppEntry.description:
One **cloud app** on the wire — the admin create/update DTO and the launch
handler's resolved shape.

The `url` is a template: `{origin}` is replaced with the served origin
at launch time, `{launch}` with a fresh per-launch nonce. A SMART-on-FHIR
app's URL might be
`https://example/launch.html?iss={origin}/fhir-r4&launch={launch}`; a
hand-rolled one might be `{origin}/some/path` or `https://other-host/x`.
See [`AppUrl`] for the accepted shapes.

subtitle.description:
The descriptive line shown under the app's name. `None` means the
row has no explicit subtitle; the UI may fall back to the URL or
render the row without one.

url.description:
The launch URL template, serialized as a plain string on the wire and
in SQLite. See [`AppUrl`] for the accepted shapes / placeholders.

AppListEntry.description:
`GET /apps` row shape — the catalogue entry. No launch `url`. See the module
docs.

provenance.description: How this app's launch target resolves; see [`Provenance`].

localOnly.description: The declared no-egress flag (a homescreen badge this pass).

smart.description: Whether this is a SMART app (the parent row carries a `client_id`).

requiresTunnel.description:
Whether a launch needs the tunnel up (cloud apps only; `false` for
system / self-hosted).

removable.description:
Whether the owner can remove this app through the admin surface: `true`
for cloud apps and for uploaded (non-seeded) self-hosted apps, `false`
for system apps and the migration-seeded self-hosted apps. The editor's
Remove control keys off this rather than re-deriving the rule per client.

AppNotEditableBody.description:
Wire shape for `AppNotEditable` (409) — the app exists but isn't a cloud app,
so the cloud-admin update/delete surface can't touch it (system + self-hosted
apps are not user-editable).

AppNotFoundBody.description: Wire shape for `AppNotFound`. Matches the TS `AppNotFoundSchema`.

CreateAppBody.description:
POST body — matches the TS `CreateAppBodySchema`. `requiresTunnel`
uses the wire-camelCase the existing client speaks. `url` is read as a raw
string so a bad value yields the structured `400 InvalidUrl` rather than a
generic deserialize error.

HomeScreenEntry.description:
One entry in the `PUT /home-screen` body: an app id and its desired `enabled`
flag. The entry's index in the array is its new display `position`. Matches
the TS `HomeScreenEntrySchema`.

InvalidFieldBody.description:
Wire shape for a 400 carrying a discriminant + human-readable reason.
Reused for `InvalidUrl` (a bad app URL), `InvalidName` (an empty name), and
`InvalidZip` (an unusable uploaded bundle) — all write-side field validations
the client renders inline. The `error` discriminant lets a client tell them
apart rather than seeing a URL-error tag for a name or upload problem.

InvalidHomeScreenBody.description:
Wire shape for a 400 `InvalidHomeScreen` — the `PUT /home-screen` body wasn't
an exact permutation of the registry (a missing, duplicated, or unknown id),
so the atomic reorder/enable can't be applied as a well-ordered whole. Matches
the TS `InvalidHomeScreenSchema`.

LaunchUnavailableBody.description:
Wire shape for a 503 `LaunchUnavailable` — a launch with no *reachable*
target (see [`HandlerError::Unavailable`]). The SPA surfaces the failure
rather than following a dead redirect / a popup pointed at an unreachable
origin.

Provenance.description:
How an app's launch target resolves. Serialized — wire + SQLite — as its
kebab string (`"system"` / `"self-hosted"` / `"cloud"`).

UpdateAppBody.description:
PATCH body — all fields optional. Matches `UpdateAppBodySchema`. The
`subtitle` tri-state is on [`SubtitlePatch`]. No `enabled`: that's homescreen
curation, owned by `PUT /home-screen`.
